key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Sudden during or shortly after aspiration event. LOCATION: Dependent lung regions (right lower lobe most common). DURATION: Acute onset, can persist for days to weeks. CHARACTER: Dyspnea, cough, chest discomfort. AGGRAVATING: Lying flat, continued aspiration risk. RELIEVING: Upright positioning, suctioning, antibiotics. TIMING: Acute, often during eating or vomiting. SEVERITY: Moderate to severe (6-8/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Fever, productive cough (may be foul-smelling), dyspnea, chest pain, altered mental status (if hypoxic). KEY POSITIVES: Recent aspiration event, fever, productive cough, dyspnea. KEY NEGATIVES: No chest pain (unless severe), no wheezing (unless reactive airway disease).
